How ip subnet is calculated

Inspect an IPv4 address and CIDR prefix to determine its network, broadcast address, mask, and usable host range. This is arithmetic for conventional IPv4 subnets; /31 and /32 have special point-to-point and host semantics, which are identified in the result. 192.168.1.10/24 belongs to 192.168.1.0/24, whose broadcast is 192.168.1.255. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. No, this tool validates dotted-decimal IPv4 only. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

network = IPv4 address AND CIDR mask
A worked example

192.168.1.10/24 belongs to 192.168.1.0/24, whose broadcast is 192.168.1.255.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does it support IPv6?

No, this tool validates dotted-decimal IPv4 only.

Why are /31 and /32 different?

They are commonly used for point-to-point links or a single address, so ordinary network/broadcast host exclusions do not apply.
